title: Why does the word for 'partners' come from a hunter's snare?

beats.narration: One word in this book began as a hunter's snare for birds. Which one?
It is the word this verse sets the speaker against. I am not of those who join others as partners with God. Partners. Co-sharers. The gravest charge in the book.

Long before, the same root named tangible things that catch and interweave. In Zuhayr's verse, ash-sharak is the fowler's snare. The net whose crossing strands cut a sandgrouse off from her sister. The word also named the interlacing tracks of a road. Paths that share one route.

poetry.arabic: كَأَنَّها مِن قَطا الأَجبابِ حَلَّأَها وِردٌ وَأَفرَدَ عَنها أُختَها الشَرَكُ
poetry.english: As though she were one of the sandgrouse of al-Ajbab, whom a watering-place had turned away — and the snare had cut her off from her sister.

beats.narration: Sharing. Interweaving. Strands that cross and catch. The book keeps that picture and aims it at the one place sharing cannot go, giving the One a co-sharer. And the snare, in the end, holds the one who set it.
